DHCPDISCOVER received on an unplugged switch port. The packet's hostname was the name you only use in dreams.
The air-gapped terminal displayed a typing indicator. A second later, someone on the other side deleted your name.
The NAS scrub found no corrupt blocks. It did find a recording of the room from inside the sealed drive bay.
The packet capture contains a valid TCP handshake with no remote host. Every payload is one frame of your bedroom door opening.
The UPS reports eleven minutes of remaining runtime. The estimate hasn't changed since the building lost power last winter.
Windows found a second face during login. The camera preview shows it slowly turning towards the first.
A new ZFS snapshot has a creation time earlier than the pool itself. Its only file is a floor plan with another room.
The serial console prints one dot whenever you blink. When you close your eyes, it prints PLEASE KEEP WATCHING.
A disconnected fibre returns light from both ends. The pulses spell the technician's childhood address.
The monitoring system reports a new rack between racks six and seven. The floor plan now shows eight metres of missing wall.
An NTP server returned a date that doesn't exist. Every clock that accepted it now counts backwards towards the same second.
The thermal camera sees a person-shaped cold patch inside the firewall appliance. It stands when someone enters the room.
A signed firmware image contains your name in the build path. The signature predates your birth.
The inactive microphone produced a waveform while physically disconnected. Listening to it makes the corridor seem longer.
The VLAN capture shows traffic from a camera assigned to a room the building never had. The feed shows you reading the capture.
The access log grants entry to the same badge every night. The badge is locked in a sealed evidence bag.
The backup verification restored one extra user profile. Every document inside is a polite request to be let out.
A Linux process keeps returning after shutdown. Its parent PID is the date your father disappeared.
The repair ticket closed itself with a photograph attached. The photograph was taken from inside the customer's closed laptop.
The router's neighbour table contains a device named OTHER_SIDE. Its MAC address changes to match whichever technician is alone.
A parity check corrected one sector. The corrected bytes spell the exact sentence you were thinking.
The inactive printer queue shows one completed job. Owner: THE OCCUPANT BEFORE YOU.
The fibre tester reports a reflection at minus twelve metres. Behind the operator, something taps the wall.
The CCTV recorder added a channel called BELOW. Its camera moves whenever you swallow.
Every SMART temperature sensor reads normal except one. It reports the temperature of a human hand pressed against the platter.
The core dump contains a clear photograph of the engineer reading it. The server has never had a camera.
The DNS query for your own name resolves to a private address. From the address, a voice asks which name you used before.
The PoE budget includes a device on a port that was removed from the board. Its power draw rises when the lights go out.
The checksum of an unchanged archive changes only when someone in the room lies. Nobody wants to try the next test.
The GPS receiver has no fix, but its altitude falls one metre every minute. The workshop floor feels softer than yesterday.
The oscilloscope displays a face on a grounded input. Increasing the timebase makes its lips move more slowly.
The support call recording has two channels. On the second, the customer answers each question before the technician asks it.
The motion detector logs a person leaving an empty room. The event repeats until someone volunteers to enter.
The write-protected floppy gained a directory overnight. Its name is the date the technician is due to retire.
The hypervisor lists a running guest using no RAM or disk. Its console shows a chair facing away from the screen.
The building sensor bus has a new address. It reports a heartbeat from inside the poured concrete.
The Bluetooth scan finds a device named DON'T PAIR. Its signal gets stronger each time you dismiss the notification.
The print server receives a job with zero pages. The preview shows a hand slowly pressing against the blank area.
The cable tester lights pin nine on an eight-contact connector. From the far room, someone says there is space for one more.
The voicemail system records a caller breathing for exactly your remaining shift. The final sound is your office door unlocking.
The screenshot tool captures a person-shaped gap in every open window. Moving a window makes something behind it complain.
The disk image mounts read-only, but the files keep renaming themselves. Together, their names form instructions for finding a hidden door.
The camera's privacy shutter is physically closed. The face detector still follows someone moving behind the technician.
The soldering station reports a second tip temperature. The cold tip is getting warmer inside the locked drawer.
A firewall drop log repeats the same source address. The address is scratched into the underside of the desk.
The display test cycles red, green, blue and a colour nobody can describe afterwards. Everyone remembers a different missing person.
The server's BMC reports the chassis open. The lid is sealed, but the room's ceiling has started separating from the walls.
A cron job runs on the thirty-second day of every month. Each run removes one face from the staff photographs.
The drone's blackbox contains a second flight overlapping the first. In that log, the aircraft follows the pilot home.
The temperature graph contains a perfect outline of the office floor plan. One room is labelled with tomorrow's date.
A MikroTik export contains a comment nobody wrote: DO NOT REMOVE THE LAST RULE. The last rule only has a comment: IT LEARNS.
The test speaker reproduces a tone below its rated range. The technician feels someone answering through the soles of his feet.
The time-lapse camera lost exactly one frame per night. The missing intervals now contain a continuous recording of someone approaching.
The log rotation compressed last night's file to one byte. Reading that byte aloud makes every locked door click.
The badge reader shows ACCESS DENIED before anyone approaches. It changes to WELCOME BACK when the room is empty.
The new network diagram includes a cable passing through the wall without a hole. Pulling either end makes the other end breathe.
The machine's uptime counter continues after the motherboard is removed. The old case makes a small sound whenever it increments.
A Python traceback ends with a line that doesn't exist in the source. The line contains the next thing the operator is going to say.
The restore job asks whether to overwrite the current occupant. The technician's account has already selected YES.
The paging system plays the night guard's final announcement every dawn. Tonight, the recording began with a request to change the ending.
